post.summary:
Email a sign-in code: the first step of creating an account and of
signing in with a code (D-59, D-60). Sending again is the same call.
The answer is the same for any address, with an account or not.

Sign in with the emailed code, making the account if the address has
none. Sets the refresh cookie. `account.completed` false: the account
must be completed before anything else (D-61).
Sign in. Sets the refresh cookie.
A new access token, from the refresh cookie. Replaces the cookie too: each is used once.
End this session. Always succeeds, and clears the cookie.

The "complete your account" step (D-61): the only way an account made
by a code or by Google gets past ACCOUNT_INCOMPLETE. The access token in
use keeps working; read `GET /users/me` again for the profile.

get.summary:
What the sign-in pages need to know: the other providers configured
(`google`).
The live sessions: this device first, then by latest use.

delete.summary:
"Sign out the other devices": every session but this one ends; they
learn why at their next request (`signed_out_everywhere`).

Sign out one session (`revoked` at its next request). The same answer
when it already ended, or is not one of yours.

post.summary: Email a code for choosing a new password. The answer is the same for any address.

Choose a new password with the emailed code. Ends every earlier session,
then signs in here: sets a new refresh cookie.
Change the password, knowing the current one. Ends every other session.

Ask to delete your own account, with the password as proof it is you.
It is deleted 14 days later unless you sign in and restore it (D-141).
Every session ends, this one included; the owner is emailed the date.

Restore an account waiting to be deleted: for the dialog shown after
signing in to one. The only route such an account may use besides
`GET /users/me`. Restoring one that is not waiting changes nothing.

parameters.name: redirect
parameters.description: A path of the web app to return to. Default `/`.

get.summary:
Sign in with another provider. Redirects to the provider, and sets a
short-lived cookie that ties its return to this browser.

Where the provider sends the browser back. Signs in and redirects to the
web app's `/auth/callback?redirect=<path>`; if it cannot, to
`/auth/callback?error=cancelled|failed|email_unverified|account_deleted`.

Also before the account is completed, and while it waits to be deleted:
the client reads `completed` and `deletes_at` to know where to go.
For the "complete your account" page, where a username is chosen (D-61).

delete.summary:
Back to the initial (S-ME-02, D-72). The profile page calls this only
once its "Undo" has run out. Without an avatar it answers the same.

get.summary: What a browser applies once signed in: theme, language, time zone… the same everywhere (REQ-AUTH-08).

patch.summary:
Save the settings sent, each on its own (S-ME-04 → S-ME-06). Naturally
idempotent, so no Idempotency-Key: a retry sets the same values, and a
retried zone change finds the zone already in use, which is no change.

The Health Check is not successful

get.summary: 503 when the database or Redis is unreachable.

Every server they are in, with the channels they may see and what they
may do there (D-115, D-145). The rail and the channel list read this.

post.summary:
A new server from a template (S-SRV-01). Answers with the server as the
list shows it, so the client adds it to the rail and opens its first
text channel without another request.
A new icon, cropped square by the client (MANAGE_SERVER).
A category at the end of the list (MANAGE_CHANNELS).

delete.summary: Its channels move above the first category (REQ-SRV-02).

post.summary: A text channel or a room at the end of its group (MANAGE_CHANNELS).

patch.summary: One drop (D-149). Declared before channels/:channelId, which would take "order" for an id.

language.description: The language of the page, for the email this sends.

created.description: Made by this sign-in: the address had no account (D-59).

completed.description:
Done the "complete your account" step. False: open it before anything
else (D-61). The gate that refuses it everywhere else comes with that
step (D-128).

access_token.description: Send as `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>`. Keep it in memory only.

expires_in.description: Seconds until it expires. Refresh shortly before.

code.description: The six digits from the email.

access_token.description: Send as `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>`. Keep it in memory only.

expires_in.description: Seconds until it expires. Refresh shortly before.

display_name.description: Shown in chat and study rooms: 1-32 characters, at least one visible (REQ-AUTH-06, D-69, D-139).

timezone.description: An IANA time zone name, e.g. `Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh`. Does not count as the day's change (D-61).

language.description: The account's language: the switch at the foot of the page (D-64).

username.description:
2-32 characters of `a-z 0-9 _ .`; upper case is lowered. Permanent.
Whether it is free is decided now: taken → USERNAME_CONFLICT.

password.description:
The password, under the rules of REQ-AUTH-01; it may not be the email,
the part before @, or this username (D-66). Refused →
AUTH_PASSWORD_REJECTED naming the rules broken.

terms_accepted.description:
"I agree to the Terms of Service and the Privacy Policy": must be true.
The value as sent: the global pipe's implicit conversion would make
the string "false" true, recording consent nobody gave.

providers.description:
The other providers configured for sign-in, by id (`google`). Empty when
none are. Start one with `GET /auth/<id>`.

browser.description: Chrome, Edge, Firefox, Safari, Opera, Cốc Cốc, Samsung Internet, Chromium; null when not one of these.

os.description: Windows, macOS, iOS, iPadOS, Android, Ubuntu, Linux, ChromeOS; null when not one of these.

ip.description:
The network of the last use, the rest masked: `14.231.x.x`,
`2405:4802:x:x…` (D-138). Null when it is not known.

last_active_at.description: The last refresh, or the sign-in before any.

current.description: The session of this request: "This device". Always first.

revoked.description: How many sessions ended: "Signed out 2 other devices".

language.description: The language of the page, for the email this sends.
The language of the page, for the email this sends.

code.description: The six digits from the email.

language.description: The language of the page, for the email this sends.

deletes_at.description:
When the account is deleted: 14 days from now. Signing in before then
offers to restore it. The sign-in page shows the date.

language.description: The language of the page, for the email this sends.

email.description: Absent only for an account whose personal data has been erased.

completed.description:
Whether the "complete your account" step is done (D-61). While it is
not, every other signed-in route answers ACCOUNT_INCOMPLETE: the client
opens /welcome.

deletes_at.description:
When the account is deleted, if its owner asked to delete it; null
otherwise (D-141). While it is set, every other signed-in route answers
ACCOUNT_PENDING_DELETION: the client offers to restore it.

display_name.description: 1-32 characters, at least one visible; it cannot be cleared (D-69).

bio.description: Up to 200 characters, line breaks allowed. An empty string clears the bio.

timezone.description: An IANA zone name, in ICU's letter case (asia/tokyo is stored as Asia/Tokyo).

timezone_changeable_at.description:
When the zone may change again (once every 24 hours); null if it may
now. Worked out by the server, so the device's clock does not matter.

phase_sound.description: The sound when a study phase ends (REQ-STUDY-06).

browser_notifications.description: Browser notifications (REQ-NOTIF-04): the main switch, then one per kind.

notification_prompt_dismissed.description: "Not now" on the prompt to turn browser notifications on (D-100).

allow_server_member_messages.description: Direct messages from people who share a server (REQ-SOCIAL-04).

administrator.description: Holds ADMINISTRATOR: sees every channel, so it is shown ticked and locked.

name.description: As typed; the channel list shows it in capitals.

permissions.description: What they may do in this channel (appendix B, steps 1–6).

view_role_ids.description: The roles that see it when private, sent only to those who may edit that; null otherwise.

category_id.description: Null: listed above the first category.

send_mode.description: `managers`: only those with MANAGE_MESSAGES may post.

permissions.description: What they may do in the server as a whole: menus and settings pages.

is_owner.description: The owner outranks every role and may do everything.

top_role_position.description: Their highest role's position, 0 with none. Roles at or above it are locked for them, unless they are the owner.

timeout_until.description: Set only while they are timed out.

welcome_channel_id.description: The text channel that gets "X joined the server"; null for none, or one they cannot see.

categories.description: Only those with a channel they can see, unless they manage channels.

channels.description: Only the ones they can see, by position; group them by category_id.

name.description: 2–100 characters, counted after composing and trimming.

template.description: Study Server or a plain one: only the channels it starts with differ.

id.description: The new category's or channel's id.

name.description: 1–100 characters, kept as typed; the list shows it in capitals.
A text channel's is stored normalised: "Hỏi Đáp Chung" → "hỏi-đáp-chung".

category_id.description: Left out or null: above the first category.

is_study_room.description: Voice rooms only: a shared Pomodoro, 25/5 to start with (D-45).

view_role_ids.description: For a private channel: the roles that see it, not @everyone.

send_mode.description: Text channels: `managers` lets only MANAGE_MESSAGES post.

is_private.description: Public again: its view roles are cleared.
